I've been farming this land in Quzhou for 45 years. I know the soil here — medium-textured, underlain by the aquifer we tap for irrigation. My wheat-maize rotation runs on 20 mu, and I keep 15 mu under cotton as a cash crop. With just my wife and me at home now, labor is a real constraint, especially come cotton-picking time.

For **wheat**, I'll use an improved semi-dwarf variety suited to the local disease pressure. I'll apply a full basal dressing before sowing and topdress at jointing. Three irrigations: one before sowing to charge the soil, one at jointing, one at grain fill. I've learned not to overwater — the aquifer level has dropped noticeably over the decades and pumping costs are real.

For **summer maize**, I direct-seed no-till right behind the combine. Hybrid seed, heavy nitrogen split between base and side-dress at V6. Two irrigations usually suffice with summer rainfall — maybe a third if August goes dry.

For **cotton**, I'll use a Bt hybrid — it's cut my pesticide runs significantly since the 1990s. Cotton demands more of me: more irrigations, topping, defoliation before harvest. At 63 I feel that labor cost in my back. I'll push some of the topping and defoliation to hire a day laborer if needed.

I'm not experimenting this year. I'll run the system I know.
